text.p: Hutchison Paging, one of three new entrants into Singapore's liberalising messaging market, said on Wednesday it wants 200,000 local subscribers within two or three years, equivalent to 20 percent of current users.

Hutchison's chief executive officer Raphael Goh told Reuters the company -- owned 40 percent by Hong Kong's Hutchison Whampoa and 30 percent each by Intraco and Teledata (Singapore) -- had so far invested Singapore $11 million in its island-wide paging network.
Singapore's paging market will be liberalised From April 1.

From that date the current monopoly, Singapore Telecommunications Ltd, must compete with Hutchison, state-owned ST Messaging and MobileOne, a consortium of Britain's Cable & Wireless, Hong Kong Telecom, Keppel Telecom and Singapore Press Holdings.
Goh said he was confident Hutchison could carve out a large chunk of the S$200 million market using an aggressive marketing strategy.
"We are serious on this. Our tariff prices as a whole are very attractive," he said in an interview.
"We want to be aggressive to reach the masses. Our minimum service pagers are targeted at the youth who don't need sophisticated services," he said.

Goh said he expected the Singapore paging market, which already has the world's highest penetration rates at more than 30 percent, to grow to 1.5 million subscribers over five years from one million now.
"The more numbers we get, the better off we will be," he said. "We expect to break even in two or three years."
In addition to aiming to create new pager users, Goh said the company was directly targeting SingTel customers and expected to eat into the existing pager market.

"Besides the estimated growth of the market to 1.5 million users, we are also looking at the existing subscribers of SingTel. We want to switch them over to our services. So potentially the market is very big," he said.
"Switching is one of our objectives. Within our plan we target about 30 percent of our market to be existing subscribers and 70 percent new subscribers," he said.
Goh said this would mean taking around 60,000 customers from SingTel over two or three years.
"If we can get more, of course, we won't stop there."
Hutchison's director of corporate planning, Wong Weng Thong, told Reuters the company aimed to lure new subscribers and old SingTel customers with low prices and a series of subsidies.
After an initial S$10 registration fee, Hutchison's basic numeric paging package will cost customers just S$9.90 a month.
This compares with SingTel's charge of S$15 a month for its comparable service. The company is also offering to pay SingTel's existing subscribers S$24 each in subsidies to switch carriers.
Goh said Hutchison's research had convinced it a a very low pricing strategy would reap rewards.
"We studied the market and found that 98 percent of the one million pager users were actually using (simple) numeric pagers, so there is a lot of potential in introducing enhanced services."
He said Hutchison would offer a series of enhanced paging services, such as secretarial services and operator-run messaging systems, at competitive rates.
"There is a lot of potential that has not really been tapped yet," he said.
-- Singapore newsroom (65 8703199)
